items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: We had worked at Harry's New York Bar in Chicago, for Floyd Town and His Men About Town.

ctx.x: And you hadn't known him in Chicago.

Never met him before. So here we were in New York, struggling with these kind of jobs. I did know a trumpet player by the name of Dick Donahue in Chicago. We had worked at Harry's New York Bar in Chicago, for Floyd Town and His Men About Town. That was another band in Chicago that gave us work.

And Donahue was the kind of trumpet player that, if you needed a first trumpet player, he was the man to get. He could do just about anything he wanted to do. And on top of that he could write. So I would make the arrangements for the band, especially the blues types, and he would just pass out all the parts. He knew how to write. At that time, I didn't.
